feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content shows real scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Writing is polished overall, but the document is slightly repetitive and could be tighter, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative with strong progression at NACo, culminating in leadership, platform modernization, and team/operations ownership.  
- Good use of scale indicators and concrete details (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, analytics stack), which boosts impact and credibility.  
- Broad but coherent skill mix spanning strategy, CMS/web execution, analytics, governance, and multimedia production.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to create more space for achievements and make structure cleaner.  
- Tighten wording and add more outcome-focused results where possible; several bullets describe responsibilities more than business impact.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); standardize serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “full-time” may be clearer than “full time” if used elsewhere. No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more concise opening, one or two concrete differentiators, and slightly less overlap with the skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with your senior value proposition and mission-driven/public-sector relevance; trim generic phrasing like “strong background in.”
- Add one concrete differentiator from recent roles, such as enterprise web modernization, digital governance, or analytics-enabled optimization.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel strategy, enterprise web modernization, digital governance, and workflow design that improves coordination across complex teams. Brings deep experience in advocacy and stakeholder communications, translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Avoid adding platform/tool specifics here; those are already covered well in later sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-level strengths rather than repeating detailed skill categories listed elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use broader, more senior phrasing: “Digital strategy & platform modernization” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation.”
- Tighten and sharpen for consistency: “Multichannel communications,” “Web platform administration,” “Editorial workflow & governance,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Replace vague or overlapping items with more distinctive strengths: “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership” is stronger than “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination.”
- Suggested version: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Multichannel communications • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial workflow & governance • Analytics & performance reporting • Content operations & systems design • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow & systems architecture” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and Technical + IT/Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” repeats Soft Skills and the header almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and 3–4 signature contributions so it complements—rather than repeats—your NACo leadership roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Lead digital strategy, Drupal platform development, and communications operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into sharper achievement-led points, e.g.:
- “Built and optimized digital workflows, analytics, and governance systems to improve cross-organizational communications coordination.”
- “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery experience.”
- Replace generic phrases like “support,” “advise,” and “deliver” with stronger verbs: led, built, launched, optimized, streamlined.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users reached, publishing time reduced, engagement gains, search success improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with NACo Director role; keep this version focused on what is newly built now.
- Drupal microsites/AI search already appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same examples verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more specific or results-based: add email open/click growth, audience growth, production volume, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten remaining bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio for advocacy programming, events, and recurring multimedia content” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video-program growth also appears in prior NACo entries; emphasize the studio build and enterprise capability here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination rather than broad ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and measurable if possible: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, cadence, or audience growth if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper point: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and speed of digital output.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” repeats the Director entry almost verbatim.
- “weekly advocacy video update” also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and Recent Projects section.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector relevance rather than repeating generic digital/content terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations for complex organizations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content strategy” to sound more senior and aligned with director/consultant-level work.
- If space allows elsewhere, add scale signals instead of generic wording here (e.g., “10,000+ page web ecosystems,” “50+ publishers,” “3.5M annual page views”) rather than in this skills block.
- Keep each line noun-based and parallel; avoid mixing leadership, messaging, and planning styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple recent role bullets; keep this section broader than the experience entries.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove lower-signal or older items unless job-relevant; keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if target roles explicitly ask for them.
- Drop “jQuery” from this topline section; it dates the profile and is better left in Technical + IT if needed.
- If space allows, add one impact cue aligned to recent work, e.g. “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ page public-sector sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; keep wording distinct.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making impact, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as outcomes-oriented: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, UX and performance optimization”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive dashboards” or “executive reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Consider grouping tools first, then capabilities second to improve scanability and reduce list fatigue.
- If you can support it elsewhere, add one measurable qualifier in experience bullets instead of here, e.g., reporting used across 10,000+ pages / 50+ publishers.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- “SEO and performance analysis” overlaps with the technical section’s “SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding”; avoid repeating all three in both places.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Make it more senior and outcomes-oriented, emphasizing production leadership rather than task-level skills.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools/tasks to scope and delivery: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event technical direction”
- If space allows, add scale/context tied to recent work: “Broadcast-quality in-house video and event production” or “Livestream and hybrid event production for advocacy and member communications.”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Video production leadership” unless hands-on editing is a target requirement.
- Keep terminology consistent with the rest of the CV: use “livestream and hybrid event production” rather than splitting “livestreaming” and “hybrid and virtual event production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; consider differentiating this one by focusing on studio/event delivery.
- “PTZ camera systems” is quite tactical; keep only if the target roles value hands-on production depth.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since recent experience is heavily Drupal-led, the item should signal depth/recency rather than read as a flat software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add level/context: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- If you want more impact, replace weaker/older tools with a qualifier instead of listing all equally: **Drupal-focused CMS leadership across enterprise, campaign and public-sector web environments**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one version more strategic and this one more tool-specific.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless you remove it from Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools most relevant to recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from basic languages to applied delivery: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group modern tooling with purpose: “Technical implementation: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope/outcome signals tied to recent work, e.g. “for Drupal microsites, analytics instrumentation, and workflow automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versions consistently; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills
- GTM may also overlap with analytics/tooling; if space is tight, move it to “Data, Analytics & Optimization” instead

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a generic tool dump. It would be stronger if grouped by function and trimmed to emphasize actual automation/system-building tools over everyday collaboration apps already implied elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to foreground systems work: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana” and move Slack/Teams to a collaboration category only if needed elsewhere.
- Consider grouping for clarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Workflow/project systems: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp.”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “workflow automation, editorial planning, and cross-team operations.”
- Prioritize tools you actively used in recent roles; drop older or less central platforms to keep the list tighter and more credible.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are low-value resume keywords unless central to a specific achievement.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant and reasonably current, but it reads as a bare vendor list. Strengthen it by signaling level of use and aligning it to the email/program leadership already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Email & engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys, Higher Logic, Mailchimp”
- If accurate, add scope/context rather than just names, e.g. “enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience engagement”
- Put the strongest/recent platform first; if Dynamics 365 is most current, keep that lead position
- Use consistent category style with other technical items; “platforms” is clearer than “systems” here

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with multiple work bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid adding outcome claims here unless they are not already covered in experience
- “Engagement” may partially duplicate Higher Logic’s implied community function; keep wording broad and concise

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and platform support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support daily operations across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs/results if available: website refresh size/timeline, livestream/event volume, weekly video cadence, audience growth, or process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce stacked clauses: split team-building, website refresh, content production, and supervision into distinct accomplishment bullets.
- Example: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate while improving cross-channel publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/early production rather than scaling.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; frame here as foundational process setup.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover digital/media growth, this item should emphasize innovation/program support and the podcast as a first.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer support role: “Produced multimedia and digital content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content advanced member engagement.
- Keep it to 1–2 lines; this is an older role, so concise impact matters more than task detail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video production here; later entries establish that progression better.
